Bill number: HB1130
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 341
 By Lowe

 HOUSE BILL 1130

 By Farmer

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to school counselors.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 3, Part 1, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a)

 (1) Subject to appropriation, the department shall allocate to each LEA

 sufficient funds for the LEA to employ one (1) full-time licensed professional

 school counselor position at each high school in the LEA that enrolls at least six

 hundred (600) students in grades ten through twelve (10-12).

 (2) If an LEA employs one (1) or more part-time licensed professional

 school counselors at a high school that enrolls at least six hundred (600)

 students in grades ten through twelve (10-12), then the LEA may use any funds

 received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to employ the part-time licensed

 professional school counselor on a full-time basis. An LEA that converts a part-

 time licensed professional school counselor position to a full-time position

 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2) satisfies the requirement in subsection (b).

 (3) If an LEA employs one (1) full-time licensed professional school

 counselor for every two hundred fifty (250) student members of the LEA, then the

 LEA may use any funds received pursuant to subdivision (a)(1) to supplant the

 cost to the LEA of employing the number of full-time licensed professional school

 counselors required to meet the specified ratio.

 (b) Each LEA shall employ one (1) full-time licensed professional school

counselor at each high school for which the LEA receives funding pursuant to this

section. This subsection (b) does not require an LEA that employs one (1) full-time

licensed professional school counselor position for every two hundred fifty (250) student

members of the LEA to employ any additional full-time licensed professional school

counselor positions beyond the number required for the LEA to meet the specified ratio.

 (c) The funds allocated to an LEA pursuant to this section are in addition to the

funds allocated to the LEA for purposes of the TISA.

 (d)

 (1) The state board may promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the roles and responsibilities required of a full-time

 licensed professional school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this

 section that exceed those required of school counselors in § 49-6-303.

 (2) The state board shall promulgate rules, in consultation with the

 department, to establish the amount of time each full-time licensed professional

 school counselor whose position is funded pursuant to this section must dedicate

 to providing high school students the preventative and developmental counseling

 services required in § 49-6-303(b), one (1) or more of the counseling and

 guidance services listed in § 49-5-302(b), and any of the services required to

 comply with any additional roles and responsibilities established by the state

 board pursuant to subdivision (d)(1); provided, that each full-time licensed

 professional school counselor must dedicate at least seventy percent (70%) of

 the counselor's time to working directly with high school students.

 SECTION 2. This act is not an appropriation of funds, and funds shall not be obligated

or expended pursuant to this act unless the funds are specifically appropriated by the general

assembly.

 SECTION 3. For purposes of promulgating rules, this act takes effect upon becoming a

law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, this act takes effect July 1, 2025, the

public welfare requiring it, and applies to the 2025-2026 school year and each school year

thereafter.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill proposes that the department provide funds to each local education agency (LEA) to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at every high school with at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12. These funds are separate from TISA allocations. LEAs that already employ one full-time counselor for every 250 student members may use these funds to cover the costs of meeting that ratio. LEAs may also use the funds to convert a part-time counselor position to a full-time position. 

LEAs must employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at every high school for which they receive this funding, unless they already meet the ratio of one counselor per 250 student members. The state board, consulting with the department, may create rules for the roles and responsibilities of these counselors that exceed existing requirements. The state board must also establish rules for how counselors allocate their time, provided that at least 70% of their time is spent working directly with high school students.

This act is not an appropriation of funds and requires specific appropriation by the general assembly. It would take effect immediately for the purpose of making rules and on July 1, 2025, for all other purposes, applying to the 2025-2026 school year and beyond.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: This bill proposes that the department provide funds to each local education agency (LEA) to employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at every high school with at least 600 students in grades 10 through 12.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the funding obligation, recipient, counselor qualifications, and enrollment threshold. The later appropriation statement supplies the funding condition.

assessments.summary_quote: LEAs may also use the funds to convert a part-time counselor position to a full-time position.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the conversion option but does not specify that the existing part-time position must be at a qualifying high school or expressly convey that conversion satisfies the employment requirement.

assessments.summary_quote: LEAs that already employ one full-time counselor for every 250 student members may use these funds to cover the costs of meeting that ratio.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the existing staffing-ratio condition and permission to offset the costs of counselors needed to meet that ratio.

assessments.summary_quote: LEAs must employ one full-time licensed professional school counselor at every high school for which they receive this funding, unless they already meet the ratio of one counselor per 250 student members.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the funded-school employment requirement and the exception for LEAs already meeting the specified staffing ratio.

assessments.summary_quote: These funds are separate from TISA allocations.
assessments.rationale: In the context of the newly provided funding, conveys that the funds are additional to TISA allocations.

assessments.summary_quote: The state board, consulting with the department, may create rules for the roles and responsibilities of these counselors that exceed existing requirements.
assessments.rationale: Conveys discretionary rulemaking, consultation, the funded counselors covered, and authority to impose responsibilities beyond existing requirements.

assessments.summary_quote: The state board must also establish rules for how counselors allocate their time, provided that at least 70% of their time is spent working directly with high school students.
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory time-allocation rules and the 70% minimum, but omits the required service categories: preventative and developmental counseling, listed counseling and guidance services, and services supporting additional board-established responsibilities.

assessments.summary_quote: This act is not an appropriation of funds and requires specific appropriation by the general assembly.
assessments.rationale: Conveys that the act itself appropriates nothing and that funding depends on a specific legislative appropriation.

assessments.summary_quote: It would take effect immediately for the purpose of making rules
assessments.rationale: Conveys immediate effectiveness upon enactment for rulemaking purposes.

assessments.summary_quote: and on July 1, 2025, for all other purposes, applying to the 2025-2026 school year and beyond.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the effective date for other purposes and application to the specified school year and subsequent years.
